title: Sync upstream architecture: CV printer object pattern
description:
## Summary

- Migrates from the original tidyverse/CSV approach to the `datadrivencv`-inspired CV printer object pattern, bringing the repo in line with upstream nstrayer/cv
- Replaces `parsing_functions.R` + `positions.csv` with `CV_printing_functions.R` and four structured CSVs (`entries.csv`, `contact_info.csv`, `text_blocks.csv`, `language_skills.csv`)
- Replaces `css/styles.css` + `css/custom_resume.css` with `dd_cv.css` + `dd_resume.css`, preserving the green colour scheme and Montserrat/Playfair Display fonts
- Removes ~91k lines of bundled `index_files/` assets (font-awesome, paged.js) now handled by R packages

## Test plan

- [ ] Run `rmarkdown::render("resume.Rmd", params = list(pdf_mode = FALSE))` and verify `resume.html` renders without errors
- [ ] Open `resume.html` in browser and check layout: green sidebar, fonts, contact info, education and experience sections
- [ ] Run `source("render_cv.R")` to verify PDF output

title: better call source(..., local=TRUE)
description:
From the documentation of `?source`, we know that the `local` argument:

>  FALSE (the default) corresponds to the user's workspace (the global environment) and TRUE to the environment from which source is called.

It means if we call `source()` without specifying `local=TRUE`, the global environment will be polluted. 

It has no differences if you just use RStudio IDE and click the knit button, as RStudio will evaluate the knit in a separate R session. 

However, if you want to knit the Rmd file via R commands, `local=TRUE` is preferred, in my opinion.

Anyway, it's a very very trivial issue, please feel free to close it if you don't think it's necessary.

Thanks.

title: Fix contact info hyperlinks
description: Hi Nick, Thanks so much for sharing your CV template! It's so well-organized and beautiful. I really love the spreadsheet approach. I noticed one small thing -- your social media icons (aside from email) don't have clickable links. This seems to be due to the fact that the hyperlinks added to the cells in `contact_info` in `strayer_cv_data` are lost when importing the data into R. I created a workaround by adding a separate column for hyperlinks within `csvs/contact_info.csv` and adding markdown hyperlink functionality to `index.Rmd`. This creates clickable links (if desired!) Of course, in order for this to work with the googlesheets workflow you'll have to add the "link" column (see example below). Not sure if you even wanted your contact info to be clickable, but if you do I hope this is useful! Thanks again so much for sharing your code. My CV is in dire need of beautification and your resources are incredibly helpful! Best, Brendan

title: Switch to googlesheets
description:
As I get older and more crotchety I find it more and more difficult to manually update a CSV. In response to this, I have moved the data-storing mechanism from a plain CSV to google sheets using the wonderful `googlesheets4` package. This allows for a much more easy updating system and also makes it easy to store all the other info that didn't feel write to put into a CSV before (like the intro and aside text) right with everything as separate pages/sheets within the main sheet. 

I have attempted to keep the whole thing as easy as possible to understand and modify by using a publically available sheet and preserving the old CSV driven way behind a boolean variable that can be set in the setup chunk.

title: Added a skill bar chart
description: Inspired by a fork of this template I turned the skills section from a simple list to a bar chart of relative skill.

title: Migrating to glue data
description: Simplified the workflow for going from tabular position data to markdown by removing the use of `dplyr::nest()` and `purrr::walk()` in favor of just using `glue::glue_data()` which let's me pass a single column. This makes extending the template a lot easier.
